text: CT and GLM: matched controls, independent checks and grid/time convergence Compare CT and GLM discretizations with a matched flux family, LLF coefficient, time steps and fixed physical damping. Use a constructed smooth exact solution and independent Athena++ results to separate spatial, time-integration and reference differences. These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-mhd-convergence-2026-11-22 from the ZIP. This command executes all 3 fixed cases in the supplement. Choose a new or empty output directory. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. CT and GLM: mesh/time convergence of a moving magnetostatic equilibrium Use a constructed exact equilibrium with nonzero magnetic force balanced by a pressure gradient, matching CT/GLM initial cell states, flux speed bound and time-step sequence. Methods, equations, figures and references Input and validation protocol history · Initial input Assumptions, units and boundaries Periodic unit square, gamma5/3, mu0=1, planar MHD. A=.05[cos2pi(x−.3t)+cos2pi(y−.2t)], B=(Ay,−Ax), rho1, v=(.3,.2), p=.1+(2pi)²A²/2 at t=.1. Compare analytic conserved cell averages. This is a constructed verification case, not a claimed published standard benchmark. Editorial clarification This translating smooth equilibrium is an exact solution constructed for the Atlas. Compare conserved cell averages, distinguishing pressure recovered from them from the exact cell average of pressure. A separate time integrator on the same spatial semidiscretization checks time error; it is not an independent PDE solver. Adopted numerical method Both use piecewise constants, the same fixed Rusanov speed alpha3 and forward Euler. CT uses face B/shared arithmetic corner EMFs; GLM uses cell B/psi with fixed ch3 and physical damping rate kappa2. All meshes use384 steps and identical CT/GLM dt sequences; initial reconstructed CT cell B matches GLM cell B. Orszag–Tang: matched CT/GLM and converged independent references Run CT/GLM with the same OT initial cell averages and dt sequence, comparing with separately executed Athena++ references whose mesh/time sensitivities are separated. Methods, equations, figures and references Input and validation protocol history · Initial input Assumptions, units and boundaries Standard periodic OT: gamma5/3, rho25/(36pi), p5/(12pi), v=(−sin2piy,sin2pix), B=(−sin2piy,sin4pix)/sqrt(4pi), t=.05. Both methods share192 steps on16²/32²/64². This supplements the previous immutable release. Editorial clarification Match the flux family, signal bound, time steps and physical damping, while retaining intrinsic differences in face versus cell magnetic fields and normal-field treatment. Compare the whole discretizations; do not attribute every difference solely to divergence control. Report native CT face divergence separately from a common cell-centered divergence. Adopted numerical method Primary runs use fixed alpha=ch=3 Rusanov/forward Euler and grid-independent GLM kappa2. Independent C++ Athena++ uses HLLD/PLM/RK2/upwind CT. Initial-constraint preservation by CT and active GLM cleaning: nonphysical control Intentionally begin with the same non-solenoidal cell B, checking that CT does not remove the initial defect and calibrating GLM’s B/psi response. This diagnostic adds no physical problem. Methods, equations, figures and references Input and validation protocol history · Initial input Assumptions, units and boundaries Periodic32² grid,t=.1,128 steps,rho=p=1,v=0,By=psi=0. CT faceBx=.01cos[2pi(i+1)/32]; GLM cellBx equals the adjacent-face average. The intentional nonzero native CT divergence violates valid physical CT initial data and is treated solely as a diagnostic. Editorial clarification This diagnostic deliberately violates the divergence constraint while giving both methods the same initial cell magnetic field. It is separate from legitimate divergence-free CT initial data and checks CT preservation of an existing constraint error. Compare GLM with an undamped control using magnetic-plus-psi wave energy, distinguishing wave phase and numerical diffusion from physical damping. Adopted numerical method Use the same fully coupled MHD code. With y-invariance andBy=vy=0, the GLM Bx/psi subsystem decouples from fluid feedback, allowing a separately constructed2x2 discrete Fourier symbol and forward-Euler matrix power. Compare kappa2/0 at identical dt and LLF viscosity, separating B/psi phase exchange from physical damping. Test the kappa2/0 ratio of auxiliary wave energy W=mean(Bx²+psi²/ch²), separating FE, semidiscrete-exponential and continuum-Fourier references. Verification limits and failures Passing means correctly detecting expected CT non-removal and the calibrated GLM response, not recommending non-solenoidal CT physical initial data. W is an auxiliary diagnostic norm, distinct from conserved physical total energy E without psi. B decay includes phase exchange and LLF diffusion; damping is assessed with the kappa0 control.
